AI Weekly Digest
July 20, 2026
A few things worth knowing this week — here's what's happening in AI, in plain English.
TL;DR — Top picks this week
How sales teams use ChatGPT Work
ChatGPT Work is a tool that helps sales teams automatically create reports like pipeline briefs, meeting prep packets, forecast reviews, account plans, and diagnoses of stalled deals using their existing data. It can save salespeople time and make it easier to spot problems in deals.
How to manage AI investments in the agentic era
This guidance shows how companies can track the value they get from AI by measuring how much useful work each dollar produces, improving efficiency, and expanding important workflows. Knowing this helps finance and operations decide where AI spending brings real benefits.
The Zoom hack that says, ‘Don’t record me’
The article warns that if every meeting, casual chat, and even a date is automatically transcribed and summarized, the sheer volume of information could overwhelm people, leaving few actually reading it. This raises privacy and information‑overload concerns for all employees.
🛠️ Tools & Products
Google is renaming NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook
Google's note‑taking app, previously called NotebookLM, has been renamed Gemini Notebook. It will stay as a separate app but will work more closely with Google's Gemini and Search features. This could make it easier for employees to capture and find information across Google tools.
Read more →
Google’s AI Mode now lets you link and interact with select apps
Google has updated its AI Mode so it can not only answer questions but also perform tasks inside selected apps. This means the AI can help complete routine work directly within the applications you already use. It could save time for employees across different departments.
Read more →
Show HN: An end to end SEO audit
A post on Hacker News introduces an end‑to‑end SEO audit tool. The tool aims to review and improve a website's search‑engine performance. Using it could help increase online visibility for our company's web presence.
Read more →
Connect Your AI Agent to Any API in Plain English (No Code)
A new solution lets you connect an AI agent to any software service using plain English, without writing code. This makes it possible to link AI to external tools quickly. It could simplify automating workflows for non‑technical staff.
Read more →
How data science teams use ChatGPT Work
Data‑science groups are using a tool called ChatGPT Work to automatically create things like problem‑analysis briefs, performance summaries, KPI notes, focused studies, and specifications for dashboards, directly from their everyday data. By turning raw inputs into ready‑to‑share documents, the AI speeds up reporting and decision‑making. This could help our teams produce clearer insights faster, reducing manual effort across finance, ops, and other departments.
Read more →
🏢 Industry & Adoption
How sales teams use ChatGPT Work
ChatGPT Work is a tool that helps sales teams automatically create reports like pipeline briefs, meeting prep packets, forecast reviews, account plans, and diagnoses of stalled deals using their existing data. It can save salespeople time and make it easier to spot problems in deals.
Read more →
How to manage AI investments in the agentic era
This guidance shows how companies can track the value they get from AI by measuring how much useful work each dollar produces, improving efficiency, and expanding important workflows. Knowing this helps finance and operations decide where AI spending brings real benefits.
Read more →
A scorecard for the AI age
Sarah Friar, OpenAI’s CFO, proposes a simple scorecard that measures the value AI delivers, the cost per successful task, reliability, and how efficiently computing power is used. This helps finance and leadership decide which AI projects are worth investing in.
Read more →
How Cars24 scales conversations and builds faster with OpenAI
Cars24 has put AI‑driven voice and chat assistants into its customer‑service process, handling more than a million minutes of conversation each month. The bots help recover about 12% of customers who would otherwise be lost, and the technology is being shared with teams across the whole company. This shows how AI can boost contact efficiency and bring back potential sales, which could be useful for our own sales and support operations.
Read more →
🔬 Research
AI is more likely than humans to form biases when hiring
AI systems are increasingly used to screen résumés before a human ever sees them, but research shows they can copy existing human biases or develop new ones, potentially leading to unfair hiring decisions. HR and job candidates need to be aware of this risk to ensure a fair hiring process.
Read more →
🛡️ Safety & Policy
The Zoom hack that says, ‘Don’t record me’
The article warns that if every meeting, casual chat, and even a date is automatically transcribed and summarized, the sheer volume of information could overwhelm people, leaving few actually reading it. This raises privacy and information‑overload concerns for all employees.
Read more →
Google ordered to open Android and Search to rivals in Europe
The European Union has ordered Google to let rival AI assistants and search engines access important parts of Android and Google Search. This decision could reduce Google's control over those platforms. It may lead to more choices for the apps and search services we use at work.
Read more →
